items.stem: Someone says an AI chatbot 'knows the answer because it sounds so confident'. Why is that reasoning unreliable?

options.text: Fluent, confident wording does not guarantee correctness; models can state wrong things convincingly
options.rationale: Correct: language models optimise for plausible text, not verified truth, so confidence is not evidence.

options.text: Chatbots are always wrong, so confidence never matters
options.rationale: Overstated: chatbots are often right; the point is confidence alone does not prove it.

options.text: Only paid chatbots can be trusted
options.rationale: Inaccurate: price does not determine factual reliability.

options.text: Confidence is reliable as long as the answer is long
options.rationale: Length is not evidence of correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: language models optimise for plausible text, not verified truth, so confidence is not evidence.

items.stem: Which TWO are good habits when using a public AI chatbot for work? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Check important facts against a trustworthy source before relying on them
Avoid pasting confidential or personal data into a public tool
options.rationale: Correct: public tools may retain or expose what you enter.

options.text: Treat every answer as final and never question it
options.rationale: Unsafe: outputs can be wrong or biased.

options.text: Assume the tool has no limits because it is 'AI'
options.rationale: Overclaim: all current tools have real limits.

items.stem: Why can an AI model reflect bias even when no one intended it to?

options.text: It learns patterns from data that already contains human and historical bias
options.rationale: Correct: models absorb the biases present in their training data.
Incorrect: machines have no preferences; bias comes from data and design.

options.text: Bias only appears if the programmer is biased in the moment
options.rationale: Incorrect: bias can arise from data alone.

options.text: Models are never biased if they are large enough
options.rationale: Incorrect: scale does not remove data bias.

items.explanation: Correct: models absorb the biases present in their training data.
